Bind Projected Coordinates to a Fitted Response Field

Source: R/response_field_geometry.R
response_field_geometry.Rd

Check the coordinates used to fit a spatial response field and package them, with their CRS, into a small descriptor for raster prediction. A response field is a spatially correlated random effect on the response, separate from the kernel scales of effect. To map such a model, each raster cell needs its own field value, and the descriptor tells predict.multiScaleR() how to compute it from cell coordinates.

Usage

response_field_geometry(
  object,
  coords,
  crs,
  batch_size = 128L,
  max_memory_mb = 512
)

Arguments

object

A multiScaleR result from multiScale_optim() with the default backend = "refit", whose fitted model is one of:

  • a glmmTMB model with one shared exponential, Gaussian or Matern field, such as exp(pos + 0 | grp), and no other random effects. The family must be Gaussian, Poisson, NB2 or Gamma with a log link, or binomial with a logit link.

  • a distance-removal model with a fixed-range abundance field from fit_gdr_response_field().

coords

Numeric matrix or data frame with two finite projected coordinate columns (x, y), one row per fitting row in the original row order. Repeated locations repeat their coordinates. For glmmTMB, use the coordinates passed to glmmTMB::numFactor(), in the same units. For a distance-removal field, use exactly the coords passed to fit_gdr_response_field(). Those are block locations, which can be coarser than the survey points used for the kernel covariates.

crs

The projected CRS of coords, as an EPSG code (for example 32617) or any input accepted by sf::st_crs(). It must have two horizontal axes and linear units that match coords. Geographic, geocentric, vertical and compound CRSs are rejected. Prediction rasters must use an equivalent CRS. Nothing is transformed or rescaled, so choose the projected CRS before fitting.

batch_size

Positive integer, default 128. The largest number of raster cells passed to each native prediction call. Smaller batches use less memory but repeat the native setup more often.

max_memory_mb

Positive number, default 512. A conservative budget, in MiB, for the dense arrays of each prediction batch. A batch whose estimate exceeds the budget stops before native prediction. Lower batch_size if that happens. This is a planning estimate, not an operating-system memory cap. For a distance-removal field, the budget set in fit_gdr_response_field() also applies.

Value

A multiScaleR_field_geometry object, a small list that stores no model, coordinates or predictions. It contains:

  • schema_version, and for distance-removal fields provider ("native_GDR_fixed_range"), range and range_estimated (FALSE).

  • crs (WKT text) and units, the linear units of the CRS.

  • For glmmTMB fields, position and group, the names of the position and group columns, with the fitted group_value and group_levels.

  • training_locations (distinct field locations) and training_rows.

  • provider_version, the glmmTMB or TMB version.

  • batch_size and max_memory_mb, the prediction controls.

  • reference_sha256, binding_sha256 and definition_sha256, SHA-256 fingerprints of the coordinates, of the fitted context and of the descriptor itself. Prediction stops if any of them no longer matches, so recreate the descriptor after refitting or changing its inputs.

Map a fitted field

Pass the descriptor to predict.multiScaleR() through raster_args = list(field_geometry = geometry). Prepare the layers with kernel_scale.raster() using scale_center = TRUE and match_buffer = TRUE. Each cell then supplies its own projected coordinates to the field, and prediction runs on one core, in batches of batch_size cells. No covariance among cells is computed or stored. Several rows in raster_args$const give one band (or fit and SE pair) per scenario row, in row order.

glmmTMB fields

Every raster cell is a new field position, so set native_args = list(allow.new.levels = TRUE) in predict.multiScaleR(). Without it, prediction stops before the first batch. All cells use the single fitted field group, and a scenario that names another group stops. Supply ordinary site and offset scenarios as usual. A position or group scenario passed to kernel_scale.raster() is replaced by the cell coordinates during prediction. Do not substitute a constant coordinate. On the response scale, predictions are the expected count for Poisson and NB2 models, the mean for Gaussian and Gamma models, and the per-trial probability for binomial models, including binomial models fitted to success and failure counts.

Distance-removal fields

Use type = "lambda" for density. Each cell gets the field value predicted at its center from the fitted block values, with the range held fixed. allow.new.levels is not used. See fit_gdr_response_field() for the full workflow, including scale-of-effect estimation with the field.

What the standard errors include

Standard errors are conditional on the selected kernel scales. They include the fitted coefficient and field uncertainty, and for distance-removal fields the extra field variance between blocks. They add no observation noise and no kernel-scale uncertainty. re.form = NA gives a zero-field reference, not an average over the field. Checking the coordinates does not establish that the field is well estimated or that its intervals are calibrated.

See also

predict.multiScaleR(), kernel_scale.raster(), fit_gdr_response_field(), prediction_contract(), vignette("v11-spatial-fields", package = "multiScaleR")

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Give the bundled landscape (in meters) a projected CRS
  land <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "landscape.tif",
                                  package = "multiScaleR"))[["land2"]]
  terra::crs(land) <- "EPSG:32617"
  data("surv_pts")
  pts <- terra::vect(surv_pts)
  terra::crs(pts) <- "EPSG:32617"
  pts <- pts[seq(1, 100, by = 2)]   # 50 survey points
  xy <- terra::crds(pts)

  # Counts depend on habitat at a 400 m scale plus a correlated field
  set.seed(3)
  truth <- kernel_scale.raster(land, sigma = 400, kernel = "gaussian",
                               verbose = FALSE)
  x2 <- as.numeric(scale(terra::extract(truth, pts, ID = FALSE)[, 1]))
  field <- drop(t(chol(0.25 * exp(-as.matrix(stats::dist(xy)) / 800))) %*%
                  stats::rnorm(nrow(xy)))
  inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = land, max_D = 1200,
                        kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)
  df <- data.frame(counts = stats::rpois(nrow(xy), exp(1 + 0.6 * x2 + field)),
                   inputs$kernel_dat)
  df$pos <- glmmTMB::numFactor(xy[, 1], xy[, 2])   # field positions (m)
  df$grp <- factor("all")                          # one shared field
  m0 <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(counts ~ land2 + exp(pos + 0 | grp),
                         family = poisson(), data = df,
                         start = list(theta = c(log(0.5), log(500))))
  fit <- multiScale_optim(m0, inputs, n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)

  # Bind the fitting coordinates and their CRS to the fitted field
  geometry <- response_field_geometry(fit, coords = xy, crs = 32617)
  print(geometry$training_locations)   # 50 distinct field locations

  # Expected counts with conditional SEs for a 10 x 10 cell window
  layers <- kernel_scale.raster(land, multiScaleR = fit,
    scale_center = TRUE, match_buffer = TRUE, clamp = TRUE, verbose = FALSE,
    site_values = list(pos = as.character(df$pos[1]), grp = "all"))
  window <- terra::crop(layers, terra::ext(1500, 1700, 1500, 1700))
  attr(window, "multiScaleR_projection") <-
    attr(layers, "multiScaleR_projection")
  map <- predict(fit, window, se.fit = TRUE, uncertainty = "conditional",
                 native_args = list(allow.new.levels = TRUE),
                 raster_args = list(field_geometry = geometry))
  print(map)   # bands: fit (expected count) and se.fit
}
#> [1] 50
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 10, 10, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 20, 20  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1500, 1700, 1500, 1700  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 17N (EPSG:32617)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       :      fit,   se.fit
#> min values  : 2.103838, 0.379276
#> max values  :  3.97472, 0.585109
# }
